svg.title: Eight Dapr security capabilities protecting one application
svg.desc: A Kubernetes cluster holds the Dapr control plane along its top, each service in its own pod in the dapr-system namespace, and a state store in a redis namespace beside them, marked 8 because its data is encrypted at rest. Below are three namespaces. In namespace default a reverse proxy runs beside a Dapr sidecar, reached over SSL by a globe outside the cluster, and marked 1 for API token authentication between the app and its sidecar. In namespace A, App A runs beside a sidecar; the line reaching its sidecar from the reverse proxy is marked 2 for a service access policy and carries a shield and padlock for mTLS. In namespace B, App B runs beside a sidecar; the line reaching its sidecar from App A is marked 3 for a pub/sub topic access policy. From App B a run reaches the state store, marked 4 for a component scope policy, and an arrow runs straight down to a key marked 7 for secrets. Beside App B, 5 marks an API access policy and 6 a secret access policy.
